channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal trade sustains families as tree cutting threatens forests
item.description: A 65-year-old burner says his family relies on the work, while the environment agency warns that producers are cutting orange and mango trees.

item.title: Sierra Leone regulator reports NLE 7.4 million in 2024 revenue
item.description: The electricity and water regulator said levies and licenses generated more than the NLE 2.3 million recorded in 2023.

item.title: Sierra Leone’s vice presidency has produced no elected successor
item.description: A political analyst says the office has often balanced party blocs rather than prepared vice presidents to lead, citing Solomon Berewa’s 2007 defeat.

item.title: Tanzania and Kuwait agree to implement cooperation resolutions
item.description: Their officials named trade, investment, energy, education and health as priority areas at a virtual meeting held in Dodoma on November 26.

item.title: Abdelaziz calls for 10-year plan to reform Libya's education sector
item.description: He says more than 700,000 staff and teachers serve 1.3 million students, and argues staffing reform must protect employees' livelihoods.

item.title: Gadzi sub-prefect accused of charging for neighbourhood chief posts
item.description: Corbeau News Centrafrique reports that five or six houses now suffice to create a neighbourhood and appoint a chief, with payment demanded from those who want the post.

item.title: Magagula’s Maniema Union hosts Singida in CAF group stage
item.description: The Eswatini midfielder’s Congolese club has eight points from five matches and needs a top-four finish to reach the Championship Group.

item.title: Dakar police send two men to prosecutors over alleged same-sex relations
item.description: The 19-year-old student and a 24-year-old university student were detained in Niary Tally on 21 November, according to Libération.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau parties demand election date as military rule hits one year
item.description: Authorities postponed the December 6 vote, citing a lack of technical and logistical conditions for the poll.

item.title: Kenya's FOP proposes hanging for corruption if elected
item.description: Presidential candidate Onyango Oloo also promises informants 10% of public funds recovered through their disclosures.

item.title: Ramaphosa to deliver eulogy at Mlambo-Ngcuka’s state funeral
item.description: South Africa’s first female deputy president will receive Category 2 honours, including military ceremonies, at a service in the Eastern Cape.

item.title: Audit finds 39% compliance at Central African Republic slaughterhouses
item.description: A review of Bangui and Bouboui sites also says the operator failed to remit the state’s 25% share of revenues under its contract.

item.title: Central African Republic committee begins nationwide price checks
item.description: Created by the prime minister on 10 November, its three commissions will monitor essential goods, transport fares and petroleum supplies.

item.title: AU calls for Sudanese-led talks after Ethiopia proposes dialogue
item.description: African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf said Sudanese stakeholders should lead any talks to end the war after Ethiopia offered to convene them.

item.title: Muluzi urges Mutharika to adopt economic recovery plan
item.description: The UDF leader says foreign-exchange and fuel shortages, disrupted activity and mounting hardship demand a national response.

item.title: Port-Louis sets draw for 320 Night Market stalls after 500 applications
item.description: The 18 December market has drawn about 180 more applicants than spaces, and only traders who live in the city can apply.

item.title: Kenya rolls out biometric suspect system in Mombasa
item.description: The police say the system will match fingerprints against national records and cut clearance-certificate processing from 14 days to 15 minutes.

item.title: Rugwabiza leaves Central African Republic UN post after four and a half years
item.description: The outgoing representative cited security and institutional progress at a news conference and urged Central Africans to consolidate those gains.

item.title: Bamako court sentences merchant to 20 years for abuse of boy under 15
item.description: The Commune VI court also ordered him to pay one million CFA francs in fines and 500 CFA000 in damages to the victim.

item.title: Frelimo's Central Committee to weigh rules for internal elections and member conduct
item.description: The ruling party's Central Committee meets in Maputo province to review proposals for its 13th Congress, ahead of a code of conduct for members.

item.title: Sudan plans to mobilise 6,000 fighters on Ethiopian border
item.description: A Sudanese Special Forces official announced the plan in Gedaref State, accusing Ethiopia of assembling troops near the frontier.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea approves tools for joint population and farm censuses
item.description: The National Statistics Council approved strategic documents and questionnaires for two censuses, but members' amendments remain to be incorporated.

item.title: Lagos trains public school teachers in disaster preparedness
item.description: The state says teachers learned to identify risks, assess vulnerabilities and prepare schools for emergencies.

item.title: Air Zimbabwe signs Portuguese partner for London flights
item.description: EuroAtlantic Airways will supply a 15-year-old Airbus A330-300 after Spanish carrier Plus Ultra suspended operations amid financial difficulties.

item.title: Nyika-Vwaza trust to receive US$4 million for conservation and tourism
item.description: The funds come from a US$29.2 million conservation investment announced by the Peace Parks Foundation on November 19.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea closes first Venice Biennale appearance
item.description: The country’s pavilion at the 61st contemporary art Biennale also hosted a business meeting on investment opportunities in its market.

item.title: Morocco’s business groups seek support for exporters and farms
item.description: At talks in Rabat, the CGEM urged help for roughly 6,000 exporters, while COMADER raised farm labour shortages and food supply.

item.title: CV Interilhas seeks state ships for its maritime concession
item.description: The company says the 2023 contract amendment already provides for new vessels and requires changes to operating and financial terms.

item.title: Leer police hold five men over alleged hospital thefts
item.description: The suspects are accused of taking money, phones and other property from a hospital in Unity State, and no recoveries have been reported.

item.title: Farmers' group says Ghana's 2027 Budget leaves GH¢83.18 billion food-programme gap
item.description: The Peasant Farmers Association of Ghana says agriculture receives 3.64% of government spending, while the Feed Ghana Programme needs GH¢85.6 billion a year.

item.title: Tunisia solidarity event backs Chaima Issa and political prisoners
item.description: The Tunis gathering is part of a campaign running through 10 December, after rights groups said Issa began a hunger strike on 16 November.

item.title: South Sudan state seeks leads after more than 200 cattle go missing
item.description: The herd was attacked near Torit after being moved from Kapoeta to escape drought and food shortages in their grazing areas.

item.title: Bank of Ghana keeps Dec. 1 launch for Heritage Series notes
item.description: Governor Johnson Asiama met representatives of the families whose relatives appear on the cedi notes after public debate over a portrait.

item.title: Tanzania joins Indian Ocean states in talks on maritime security and trade
item.description: Ministers and senior officials from the Indian Ocean Rim Association are meeting in New Delhi under India's chairmanship for 2025 to 2027.

item.title: Staff at AGL Guinée and Conakry Terminal offered cancer screening through 9 December
item.description: More than 500 employees joined prevention sessions from 16 to 18 November, with urologists answering questions anonymously.

item.title: Belgium backs new UN mission mandate and presses for ceasefire compliance
item.description: Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot raised the ceasefire and the demobilisation of Rwandan Hutu rebels with the head of the United Nations mission in Congo.

item.title: Bank Windhoek raises N$650 million with JSE note
item.description: The Namibian bank drew more than N$3.3 billion in bids for its three-year senior unsecured offering, well above the amount it raised.

item.title: Cameroon opens Awae-Esse-Soa road serving 22 villages
item.description: The 82,252 km route links three communes to national roads and routes into the Central African Republic, with faster transport for farm produce.

item.title: Ghana's food imports reached GH¢36.46 billion in 2025
item.description: An opinion article says investment in irrigation, technology, finance, storage, processing and skilled workers is needed to expand domestic production.

item.title: Sudan security agents hold three Blue Nile volunteers without family or lawyer access
item.description: The General Intelligence Service arrested the community group members on November 23 over allegations of receiving funds from an activist in Uganda.

item.title: Rwanda's central bank raises key rate to 9.5%
item.description: The 75-basis-point increase follows October inflation of 19.5%, driven in part by fresh food prices up 39.9% from a year earlier.

item.title: Mauritius sets end-2028 deadline for 3G mobile networks
item.description: Operators have begun withdrawing the service on separate schedules, while the regulator requires them to protect coverage and inform subscribers.

item.title: Tunisia wins seat on chemical weapons watchdog’s executive council
item.description: The country was elected on 24 November as one of five African members for the 2027-2029 term, replacing no incumbent named in the report.

item.title: Wazalendo fighters repel rebel offensive toward Pinga in North Kivu
item.description: The Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) had attempted a new advance on the strategic town of Pinga in Walikale territory.

item.title: Mozambique's Supreme Court delays testimony in Mondlane trial until Friday
item.description: Prosecutors, the defence and a participant in the case sought further questions for the former presidential candidate before witnesses testify.

item.title: South African court sentences Zimbabwean who applied to fight for Russia
item.description: Tafadzwa Sithole pleaded guilty to foreign military assistance charges and is set to be deported to Zimbabwe.

item.title: Togo, Benin and Ivory Coast sign accord to coordinate LNG supplies
item.description: The agreement also plans cross-border gas infrastructure as Togo studies a port terminal, with no final decision announced.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea lines up banks and firms for ICAN 2026 visitors
item.description: Banks discussed foreign-currency supply and payment terminals, while wholesalers, travel agencies, hotels and telecoms firms reviewed their share of the visitor surge.

item.title: Floods wash away shacks and close roads in Gauteng and Mpumalanga
item.description: Storm damage flooded informal settlements, disrupted public services and left a bridge on the R542 near Boomplaas damaged.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau Olympic chief rejects assembly request over signatures
item.description: Fernando Arlete says only eight of the 10 required signatories qualify, disputing the judo federation's standing and the athletes' commission.

item.title: Ethiopia's EIH gives China’s TW Holding 51% of textbook venture
item.description: The proposed $30 million first phase would print, bind, package and distribute school textbooks and teachers’ guides in Ethiopia.

item.title: Standard Bank of Angola courts Chinese firms with financing pitch in Luanda
item.description: At a China Day event in Luanda, the bank brought clients and partners together to discuss funding options and Angola's economic conditions.

item.title: Kukoma Diamonds take Southern crown into national netball finals
item.description: The Blantyre club beat Tigresses 51-46 to retain its regional title and will face defending champions Blue Eagles among the national contenders.

item.title: Senegal’s parliament rejects decree imposing revised 2026 budget
item.description: The assembly adopted its resolution by 128 votes to nine, warning officials against implementing a budget it considers unconstitutional and illegal.

item.title: São Tomé firm asks court to reverse Rosema brewery ruling
item.description: The request seeks to undo the Constitutional Court ruling that restored possession, management and control of the brewery to Angola's private group RIDUX.

item.title: President faces test of his push to shape São Tomé government
item.description: The president dismissed Patrice Trovoada’s government in January 2025, citing governance failures and public dissatisfaction, a Tela Non commentary recalls.

item.title: Mauritius's Competition Commission extends cartel amnesty by three months
item.description: The Competition Commission has moved the deadline of its amnesty programme for collusive practices to 25 February 2027, from the original end date.

item.title: Benin proposes CFA174,826 billion for health in 2027
item.description: Health Minister Benjamin Ignace Bodounrin Hounkpatin told lawmakers the budget would fund emergency care, hospitals and staffing.

item.title: Mozambique's criminal investigation service seizes 334kg of methamphetamine in Vilankulo
item.description: Two Mozambican nationals were arrested after the drugs were found packed in 257 plastic boxes in a Mahindra vehicle in Inhambane province.

item.title: Senegal raises about 3 CFA000 billion on domestic markets
item.description: Public debt director Alioune Diouf said government securities supplied about 2 CFA500 billion, while regional public offerings brought in about 640 billion.

item.title: MSF adds 52-bed paediatric building at Bossangoa hospital
item.description: The 343-square-metre ward was built to handle the seasonal influx of children with malaria and malnutrition in northern Central African Republic.

item.title: Cairo airport adds international driving permit service
item.description: Travelers can complete applications at Terminal 3 or Air Mall before departure, avoiding a separate trip to outside offices.

item.title: Boakai signs US$5.7 billion Bea Mountain infrastructure deal
item.description: The agreement covers four power plants, reservoirs and more than 300 kilometres of transmission lines, after months of negotiation.

item.title: Cameroon funds 62.6% of public investment from domestic resources
item.description: Finance Minister Louis Paul Motaze told lawmakers that domestic allocations rose by CFA261 billion in 2025 while external funding fell by CFA13.9 billion.

item.title: 11 UNC cadres disavow Kamerhe’s remarks on eastern war
item.description: They say his questions about military spending and the war do not represent the party, while UNC’s leadership disputes their group’s standing.

item.title: Kiir orders forces to clear roadblocks on aid routes
item.description: A November 25 order also bars unauthorised fees that delay humanitarian convoys and diplomatic shipments moving across South Sudan.

item.title: Japanese scholar urges Tanzania to protect open sea routes and shared rules
item.description: Masayuki Tadokoro linked secure maritime trade to prosperity and urged cooperation that protects smaller countries as well as restraining powerful ones.

item.title: Nigeria’s police suspend wanted declaration against Obaigbena and eight others
item.description: Inspector-General Olatunji Disu transferred the case to the Force Intelligence Department and ordered the nine individuals to report in Abuja by November 30.

item.title: Zambia's new proportional MPs call for scrapping presidential term limits
item.description: In their maiden parliamentary speeches, some of the newly seated legislators urged the removal of presidential term limits, a position Lusaka Times says raises doubts.

item.title: Hichilema orders Zambia's councils to draft growth strategies
item.description: The president says local authorities must become active drivers of investment, enterprise and jobs under the Grow Zambia Agenda.

item.title: Botswana businesses face 72-hour data breach reporting window
item.description: Under the Data Protection Act, controllers must alert the commission without undue delay, and high-risk breaches also require notice to affected people.

item.title: Chad hands six Kouba fire suspects to justice
item.description: Authorities say the 20 November blaze burned a large area of bush in the Salamat province village.

item.title: Sierra Leone teachers threaten December 16 strike over pay
item.description: Union executive member Foday Kuyateh rejects the Government’s proposed 50% salary increase spread over three years as inadequate.

item.title: ECOWAS gives Gambia election bodies US$480,000
item.description: The electoral commission will use its share to train 8,851 polling staff ahead of the December 5 presidential election.

item.title: Sonatrach subsidiary launches flight academy for pilot training
item.description: Tassili Travail Aérien opens applications for three licensed courses beginning in early 2027.

item.title: Mauritius court sentences Vedanand Seetul to 36 years in prison
item.description: A jury found the 52-year-old guilty by seven votes to two over his wife’s death in Lallmatie in 2018.

item.title: Botswana's Orange Summer Challenge advances four AI business finalists
item.description: The teams were selected from 361 entries and developed products with commercial potential, including customer-service tools and a Setswana voice contact centre.

item.title: Guinea learns U15 school football opponents and qualification routes
item.description: The boys face four teams, while the girls must finish first in a three-team group to reach the African finals.

item.title: Namibia sets aside N$26m to pay drought-relief suppliers
item.description: The mid-year budget review directs the money to transporters and suppliers who delivered aid during the previous drought but remain unpaid.

item.title: Mauritius opens 2027 salary talks as inflation reaches 4,3 %
item.description: The first technical meeting is set for Friday 27 November, with Statistics Mauritius presenting its 2026 inflation data and projections.

item.title: Boakai signs US$5.7 billion Bea Mountain infrastructure deal
item.description: The agreement funds four power plants, grid upgrades and 14 road and bridge projects, with new company revenue earmarked for costs from 2027.

item.title: Wau security restrictions keep some voters from registration
item.description: South Sudan’s elections commission says some centres lack materials, with the nationwide registration period ending on November 28.

item.title: Ruto orders breastfeeding rooms and flexible hours at State House
item.description: The president directed staff to make spaces for mothers after Kenya signed a law on workplace support for pregnant and breastfeeding women.

item.title: Malawi launches 16 days of action against gender-based violence
item.description: Two national action plans are intended to protect women and girls, while First Lady Gertrude Mutharika called for stronger safeguards and justice for survivors.

item.title: Tunis examines plans to renovate Habib-Bourguiba Avenue
item.description: Proposals cover pavements, green spaces, lighting and pedestrian movement, but the municipality has announced neither a budget nor a construction timetable.

item.title: Namibia’s treasury bills offer savers yields up to about 8.01%
item.description: The government securities mature in 91 to 365 days, and individuals pay no tax on their interest.

item.title: Taylor seeks separate trial and Feika’s removal from US$317 million case
item.description: The former vice president’s lawyers filed both motions as pretrial proceedings began in the cocaine trafficking prosecution involving 20 defendants.

item.title: Madagascar lawmakers elect Marco Tsaradia Assembly president with 129 votes
item.description: The former supporter of Andry Rajoelina ran unopposed after other candidates withdrew and Firaisankina lawmakers left the chamber before voting.

item.title: Madagascar's government and parliament face decision on whistleblower bill
item.description: The draft protecting whistleblowers, corruption reporters and witnesses is complete, but its adoption depends on government and parliamentary bodies.

item.title: Niamey requires permits for new religious-site construction
item.description: An order signed on 17 November also gives existing sites six months to have their situation examined by city services.

item.title: Bujumbura women who beg ask government for start-up capital
item.description: Charlotte Nijimbere and other women say small grants and support to start businesses would help them leave the streets and regain independence.

item.title: AES officials prepare shared migration policies for three states
item.description: Officials from Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are discussing joint assistance for migrants and a common position in international forums.

item.title: Congo's Katanga mining firm SOMIKA backs local mineral processing
item.description: The Société Minière du Katanga joined the first Makutano Mining forum in Kinshasa, where it promoted processing minerals in the country.

item.title: Malawi Parliament summons Egenco and Escom over K2.6 billion debt
item.description: The committee wants Egenco to explain its K2.6 billion payment to outside lawyers and Escom to account for waiting before paying the debt.

item.title: Ethiopia offers bondholders $880 million in new debt for $1 billion
item.description: The exchange cuts principal by 12%, pays missed interest and offers investors a $5 fee for valid instructions before December 11.

item.title: Liberia's state oil firm puts storage expansion at US$35 million
item.description: The company says it will fund US$15 million from internal resources and borrow US$20 million, after senators questioned whether the loan had approval.

item.title: Japan sets January start for new Karuma Bridge
item.description: Ambassador Sasayama said construction is scheduled to begin on January 14, 2027, and Japan is planning a second phase of the Kampala Flyover.

item.title: Nandi-Ndaitwah demands faster action on 34 forum directives
item.description: The president says the country must move from commitments to measurable results, with the first forum's 34 commitments now under review.

item.title: Mulder’s 100 and seven wickets power South Africa to 2-0 series win
item.description: The all-rounder became the first South African to score a century and take seven wickets in one Test innings, beating Bangladesh in Centurion.

item.title: Cocoa union demands names of beneficiaries of 291 milliards FCFA stock buyout
item.description: The Syndicat national agricole pour le progrès de Côte d’Ivoire (SYNAP-CI) says the regulator has not disclosed who received state funds for removing 100 000 tonnes of beans.
